title: Render Cycle
definition: The React Render Cycle is the multi-step process React goes through to determine what the UI should look like and update the actual DOM in the browser.
simpleExplanation: Imagine you are a chef. The Render Cycle has 3 steps. 1. Trigger: The waiter hands you an order ticket (State changed). 2. Render: You look at the recipe and gather the ingredients in the kitchen (React calls your component function and figures out what the Virtual DOM should look like). 3. Commit: You place the finished plate on the customer's table (React physically updates the HTML in the browser so the user can see it).
realWorldExample: When a user clicks "Like", state changes to `likes: 1`. React triggers a render. React calls `Post()` and sees it returned `<button>Like 1</button>`. React compares this to the old button (Render Phase). Finally, React reaches into the DOM and changes the text (Commit Phase).

answers.question: Does "Rendering" mean updating the browser screen?
answers.answer: NO! This is the biggest misconception in React. "Rendering" purely means React is calling your function to see what the UI *should* look like. Updating the screen is called "Mounting" or "Committing".

answers.question: If a component renders but nothing changed, does the DOM update?
answers.answer: No. React compares the new Virtual DOM to the old Virtual DOM. If they are exactly the same, React skips the Commit phase entirely and touches nothing in the browser.

answers.question: Why must the Render Phase be Pure?
answers.answer: Because React can call your component function multiple times, abort it, or pause it (especially in Strict Mode or Concurrent Mode). If your component mutates an external variable or fetches data during render, it will cause unpredictable bugs.
